interactions.summary: A student reads Ugolino's prison dream, the starvation of the father and sons, the children's pleas, and the grotesque aftermath in which fasting outlasts grief.
Jiang identifies Ugolino as a famous Italian strategist and uses the episode to pivot toward a broader paradox about babies, innocence, and inconsistent placement across the afterlife.

speaker_notes.note: The ASR degrades heavily in Jiang's transition after Ugolino; the stable point is that he is using the children and innocence problem to surface another Dantean paradox.

claims.claim: The Ugolino passage stages treachery through the starvation of children alongside the father, making the punishment unbearable not only politically but familially.
claims.temporal_scope: Quoted Inferno material read in class on 2026-06-24.

claims.claim: Jiang identifies Count Ugolino as one of the most famous Italians of the period and as a great military strategist, which is why the episode lands as major political material rather than a random horror scene.
Jiang uses the Ugolino scene to reopen a paradox about babies, innocence, and where children belong in Dante's afterlife architecture.

signature_moments.moment: The tale culminates in the brutal line that fasting proved stronger than grief.
signature_moments.source_phrase: fasting had more force than grief
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It preserves the unforgettable compression of bodily desperation, paternal failure, and infernal memory that makes Ugolino one of Dante's signature scenes.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The famous Pisan political figure whose prison starvation story becomes the center of this canto sequence.

chronology_notes.note: After the Ugolino reading, Jiang immediately folds the scene into a broader running lecture concern about innocence, children, and contradictory afterlife placements.

uncertainty_notes.note: The post-reading transition is partially garbled, so the semantic pass captures only the secure throughline: Jiang is pivoting from Ugolino to a paradox involving babies and afterlife placement.
